description:
FILED s455 (Fable, round-13 merge review) ruling AF ask 2. In a RANGE topic loop $_ is always a raw INTEGER, so print/say of $_ cannot enter a user "" overload handler through $_ itself -- the residual entry is an overloaded object in ANOTHER printed operand, a tied $, / $\ FETCH, or a tied output handle, each of which could read the GLOBAL $_ (which works raw) or write through its box (perl-fatal in a range loop: $_ is read-only there, probed s455). BAR if taken: add print/say to %TOPIC_RAW_WORD behind the raw-topic gate; probe set = overloaded object as a second print operand inside a raw topic loop, tied $, and $\ with FETCH reading/writing $_, tied handle PRINT; bench a print-loop row before/after; PCL_OPT=none equivalence; guard rows in raw-verdict-coverage-01.t. Owner: round-14 perf filler. Context: Pl/Parser2.pm %TOPIC_RAW_WORD (the NOT-list comment names the exclusion), faster-codegen-suggestions Â§13.1.
------------------------------------------------------------------------
MEASURED s457aj (Opus agent AJ, round 14) -- the measurement half, per the
launch instruction "measure, record, implement ONLY if the probes are clean
AND the diff is small".  THE PROBES ARE NOT CLEAN AND THE PRIZE IS SMALL:

*** RECOMMENDATION: DO NOT ADD print/say/printf. ***  Experimental change made
(three words appended to %TOPIC_RAW_WORD), measured, and REVERTED; nothing in
the s457aj commit touches Parser2's allowlist.

1. THE RULING'S PREMISE IS WRONG, and it is the load-bearing half.  s455 says
   "$_ is read-only there, probed s455".  It is NOT: `for (1..N)` iterates
   FRESH MUTABLE SVs in perl, so
       eval { for (1..2) { $_ = "D" } 1 }        -> succeeds
       for (1..2) { print writer(), ";" }        -> "wrote:W;wrote:W;"
   (probed 5.40.3).  A handler reached from the body may therefore WRITE $_
   and perl keeps the write for the rest of that iteration.  So the divergence
   is silent-vs-silent, not fatal-vs-silent.

2. A PROBE MOVES FROM AGREEING WITH PERL TO DIVERGING.  `""` overload handler
   reached from print inside a raw-topic loop, writing $_ and then reading it:
       package Ov; use overload '""' =>
         sub { eval { $_ = "clobber" }; "OV(" . ($@ ? "RO" : "rw") . ":$_)" };
       for (1..2) { print Ov->new, ";" }
   perl  OV(rw:clobber);OV(rw:clobber);
   base  OV(rw:clobber);OV(rw:clobber);   <- agrees today
   +print OV(rw:1);OV(rw:2);              <- the write is silently lost
   The raw arm dynamically binds $_ to the raw counter, so the handler's write
   lands on the raw slot and the next read sees the loop value.

3. IT IS THE SAME RESIDUE THE GATE ALREADY ACCEPTS -- reached by one more word.
   The identical loss happens TODAY through `uc`, which IS on the allowlist:
       for (1..2) { my $u = uc($o); push @seen, "$u/$_" }
   perl `OV/clobber OV/clobber`, PCL (base AND +print) `OV/1 OV/2`.  So this is
   not a NEW class -- it is the documented residue in _topic_raw_ok's header
   ("an operator that finds an overload handler on a blessed operand ...
   Nothing in the four corpora does").  But `print` is by far the most common
   word in a topic loop, so adding it widens the exposure far more than any
   other single entry would.

4. THE OTHER TWO PROBE FAMILIES ARE CLEAN, and one CANNOT be asked:
   * a `""` handler that only READS $_ -- identical under both regimes
     (`OV<1>:1;OV<2>:2;OV<3>:3;`): the raw arm keeps $_'s NAME and its dynamic
     binding, and every read coerces.
   * a tied `$,` whose FETCH reads $_ -- identical (`a[1]ba[2]ba[3]b`).
   * a tied output HANDLE (`tie *OUT, 'TH'`) -- CANNOT DISCRIMINATE: PCL dies
     "tie: a non-lvalue (class TH) is not implemented" (#155) before the
     question is reached.  Whoever revisits this must close #155 first or say
     out loud that the leg is unmeasured.
   * the plain shapes (`for (1..5) { print }`, `print $_, ","`, `print "$_-"`,
     `for ('a'..'e') { print }`, print mixed with an accumulator) -- all
     identical under both regimes.

5. THE PRIZE IS 13% OF A 4.8x GAP.  `for (1 .. 2_000_000) { print $null $_ }`
   (output to /dev/null), two runs each, SIBLING AGENT ACTIVE on the machine so
   treat the absolutes as indicative -- the ratio is fair (same machine, same
   minute):
       perl            0.13 s
       PCL base        0.63 s   (4.8x)
       PCL +print      0.55 s   (4.2x)
   The box allocation is not what makes a print loop slow; the print path is.
   A heavier body shrinks the fraction further.

6. EMISSION REACH: ZERO.  corpus-diff with the three words added is IDENTICAL
   across all 111 files + shapes -- no file in the measured corpus takes the
   new arm at all.

IF IT IS TAKEN ANYWAY (a future ruling may decide the residue is acceptable):
the diff really is three words in %TOPIC_RAW_WORD and its NOT-list comment; the
bar is then #155 first (so the tied-handle leg can be measured), the probe set
above as guard rows in raw-verdict-coverage-01.t including probe 2 as a KNOWN
divergence row, and a not-supported.md line naming the widened residue.


=== CLOSED (s473r, 2026-09-07) ===
Flipped to completed WITHOUT re-measuring: this lever was MEASURED AND DECLINED
before the round-31 brief listed it (DECIDED grep "#813 MEASURED AND DECLINED").
The change was made, measured (for (1..2e6) { print $null $_ } 0.63 -> 0.55 s,
4.8x -> 4.2x of perl) and REVERTED, because the s455 premise it rested on is
false: `$_` in a range loop is a fresh MUTABLE SV in perl, so the raw arm loses
a handler`s write to $_.  Emission reach over the 111-file corpus was ZERO.
The re-open condition in the text above stands; re-measuring a ruled decline is
waste (s473r brief, "THREE LEVERS ARE ALREADY MEASURED AND DECLINED").
